title: Disambiguate a rule that reads two ways
statement: When a content rule can be read two ways, add a one-line disambiguation and an example of what it does and doesn't forbid.
example: In an audit against 325 rules, one rule read the wrong way would have made every card of one kind in the shipped course defective.
detail: A Grade 3 lesson was audited against a nine-document rulebook, 325 rules in all, by nine independent rule-by-rule audits, an adversarial pass on every serious finding and a re-check of each one that survived. One rule, that a vocabulary card's example never contains the target word, was read by a careful audit as never containing the word being defined, which would have made every card of that kind in the shipped course defective; the intended meaning was another card's taught word. The verdict counted it among four problems in the rulebook itself and asked for a one-line disambiguation with an example.

evidence.quote: 04 §3's *"The example never contains the target word"* was read by a careful auditor as *"never contains the word being defined"* — which would make **every V3 card in the shipped course** defective.
This needs a one-line disambiguation and an example
